result.title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models
result.comment: Accepted to AXIOM: Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning (NeurIPS 2026 workshop). 4 pages + appendix, 4 figures, 5 tables
result.summary: Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale. We present the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study of a spiking language model, sweeping SpikeGPT-family models (RWKV backbone) from width 384 to 1536 across compute budgets from $3\times10^{17}$ to $10^{19}$ FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. We report two findings. First, the compute-optimal frontier is $N_{opt} \propto C^{0.56}$, close to the 0.50 that Hoffmann et al. report for dense Transformers, so spiking does not change how parameters and data should be traded off under a compute budget. Second, against non-spiking RWKV and Transformer baselines trained the same way, the loss gap splits into a backbone cost of about 0.16 nats that does not change with compute and a spiking cost that falls from 0.34 to about 0.23 nats and then levels off. These results give the first compute-optimal recipe for spiking language models and quantify the accuracy cost of their sparsity.

AI.brief_summary: 首次对 SpikeGPT 族脉冲语言模型做 Chinchilla 式 IsoFLOP 缩放研究，拟合计算最优的参数量—数据配比，并把损失差距拆为不随算力变化的骨干成本与逐步收敛的脉冲化成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 IsoFLOP 扫描与损失分解量化「额外计算／稀疏化」代价的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理步数带来的算力—精度权衡与成本归因提供可核查的方法模板，但本身不涉及视觉或多模态状态。
